The "Investiture of the Gods" records how Lord Jiang obtained the divine register with the assistance of deities such as the Primordial Heavenly Venerable, Taiyi Zhenren, and the Southern Immortal Elder.

Congratulations on obtaining this supreme auspicious omen! Like the dragon and tiger meeting with wind and clouds, your great aspirations will be fulfilled, and you will reach the realm of ultimate goodness and joy. This signifies success in all directions, favorable circumstances everywhere, and everything going according to your wishes.

title: Divine Omen No. 04

Divine Omen No. 04: Dong Yong Meets the Immortal
Omen Fortune: Moderately Auspicious Omen

Divine Omen Poem:
Young purple swallows at the eaves,
Chattering softly near noon.
Coming and going, low then high,
Sometimes cutting through green willow mist.

Historical Context:
Dong Yong, a native of Qiancheng, lost his mother young and was left to care for his father alone. He wandered to Xiaogan. When his father died, he had no money for burial, so he borrowed ten thousand coins from someone. Later, having no money to repay, he was to become a slave. One day while cutting firewood on the mountain, he fell asleep exhausted. Heaven, seeing his filial piety, sent down an immortal maiden to marry him.

When Dong Yong woke and saw the woman, he feared she was a demon. The woman stopped him, saying she had no parents and no support, and wanted to become husband and wife. Dong Yong, seeing her pitiful state, took her home. His master blamed Dong Yong for abducting a woman, which would bring disaster to his master. Later, they temporarily kept the woman and searched everywhere for families who had lost a woman. Only then did they allow the marriage.

The immortal wife wove fifty zhang of brocade in a hundred days. She cut half to sell at the market for silver to redeem Dong Yong's freedom. Later, she presented the brocade and was granted the title of "Treasure Presenting Scholar."

Divine Fortune Interpretation:
This divine omen describes the natural scenery that Dong Yong and the immortal maiden saw in spring. Swallows shuttling back and forth at the eaves, searching for food, returning to the nest to feed the next generation. It's comforting that swallows, to nurture the next generation, will definitely choose safer environments to build nests. The first two lines show the mother swallow chattering softly with her young at the eaves, indicating signs of peace.

The last two lines of the omen remind us that the young swallows' parents, in search of food, come and go, sometimes high sometimes low, suggesting fortunes that rise and fall, sometimes good sometimes bad, with fluctuations throughout the year.
